question: How do I create a kMeet meeting?
ground_truth: To create a kMeet meeting: 1) Start kMeet via kmeet.infomaniak.com or from the desktop/mobile app. 2) Start a new meeting. 3) Enter a name for your meeting room. 4) Allow access to webcam and microphone. 5) Enter your name or pseudonym. 6) Optionally enable participant control, password, or encryption. 7) Click 'Join the meeting'. 8) Share the room link to invite participants.
actual_response:
To create a kMeet meeting, follow these steps:

### Prerequisites:
- You must have access to kMeet via [kmeet.infomaniak.com](https://kmeet.infomaniak.com) or the kMeet application for computers or mobile devices.

### Steps to Create a kMeet Meeting:
1. Start kMeet via [kmeet.infomaniak.com](https://kmeet.infomaniak.com) or from the kMeet application.
2. Click the button to start a new meeting.
3. Enter a name for your meeting room.
4. Allow access to your webcam and microphone if prompted.
5. Enter a pseudonym or your first and last name.
6. Optionally, enable participant control, set a password, or use a custom encryption key for added security.
7. Click **Join the meeting**.
8. Share the meeting link with participants to invite them to join.

### Additional Features:
- You can create a meeting room in advance and invite participants by creating an associated event in the Infomaniak calendar. For more details, refer to [this guide](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/956).
- It is also possible to share the video stream within a Video Streaming Broadcast.

### User Role Requirements:
- To manage participants or create side rooms, you must be a moderator.

### Technical Specifications:
- There is no limit to the number of participants with paid kSuite offers.

### Related Actions:
- You can manage participants, create side rooms, or secure the meeting with a password or encryption key.

For more details, refer to the [official documentation](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2475/create-a-kmeet-meeting).

question: How can I share my screen during a kMeet call?
ground_truth: To share your screen in kMeet: 1) Have the desktop app (macOS/Windows) or mobile app (Android) - screen sharing is not yet available on iOS. 2) Create or join a meeting. 3) Click on the screen icon with an arrow to 'Share your screen'. 4) Validate authorization to access screen content. 5) Choose to share the entire screen or a specific window. 6) Click button to start sharing. 7) To stop, click the toolbar icon again. Note: Permissions may require a restart on first use.
key_points: choose entire screen or specific window
actual_response:
To share your screen during a kMeet call, follow these steps:

### Prerequisites
- You must have the **desktop** app kMeet (desktop application on macOS / Windows) or the **mobile** kMeet app (application for smartphone or tablet **Android**). The Web kMeet app (online service kmeet.infomaniak.com) is also compatible.
- Screen sharing is not yet possible with the mobile iOS app.
- If this is your first use or first screen share, the permissions requested by the operating system (macOS, Windows...) or the browser (Chrome, Firefox...) may require a **restart** of the application and consequently an interruption of the meeting.

### Steps to Share Your Screen
1. Start kMeet via [kmeet.infomaniak.com](https://kmeet.infomaniak.com) or from one of the applications for computers or mobile devices.
2. Create or join a meeting room.
3. Click on the screen icon with an arrow to **Share your screen**.
4. Read the warning that may be displayed by your device and validate the authorization to access the screen content.
5. By default, it is the **entire** screen that will be shared in the next step, but you can also choose a **specific window**, that of an application for example, in order to restrict the participants' view to a specific activity of the device. Be careful, if the purpose of the sharing is to then allow participants to interact by drawing, you must choose to share the full screen.
6. Click the button to start the **sharing**.
7. To stop the broadcast, click again on the toolbar icon.

### Important Notes
- If you plan to allow participants to draw on your screen, ensure you share the entire screen, not just a specific window.
- Prepare the technical aspects in advance to avoid interruptions during the meeting.

For more details, refer to the [official guide](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2477/share-your-screen-on-kmeet).

question: What should I do if my audio is not working in kMeet?
ground_truth: To fix audio issues in kMeet: 1) Go to kMeet Settings and reauthorize microphone access. 2) Check browser lock icon isn't blocking multimedia. 3) On mobile, check Settings > Privacy > Microphone permissions for kMeet. 4) On Windows, use Privacy settings and Audio Troubleshooter. 5) Try joining from a different device (mobile instead of computer or vice versa). 6) As last resort on Firefox, disable WebRTC in about:config by setting media.peerconnection.enabled to false.
actual_response:
If you are experiencing audio issues in kMeet, follow these troubleshooting steps:

### 1. (Re)authorize Multimedia Access
- Go to the kMeet **Settings** (click on the icon at the top right of the interface).
- Reactivate the requests for permission to access multimedia functions:
  - Access to a microphone (choose the device that suits you).
  - Access to the camera if available.
- Check that a **lock** in your browser's address bar is not blocking your multimedia access by clicking on the lock.

### 2. Windows Troubleshooter for Audio Issues
- Access the **Windows settings** section **Privacy**.
- Ensure the following access permissions are enabled:
  - "Allow apps to access the camera."
  - "Choose which Microsoft Store apps can access the camera."
- Enable 'Windows Search', 'Camera', and 'App Connector'.
- For the microphone, follow the same steps.
- If the issue persists:
  - Go to **Search** in the taskbar, type **Audio Troubleshooter**, then select **Find and fix problems playing sound** from the results to launch the troubleshooter.
  - Select **Next**, then choose the device you want to troubleshoot, and proceed with the troubleshooter.

### 3. Join the Ongoing Meeting with a Different Device
- If you encounter audio/video issues during a kMeet meeting, join it from a different device (e.g., switch from a computer to a mobile device or vice versa).
- On the ongoing meeting with the problematic device, invite a new participant to get the meeting link.
- From a new device, open a web browser (Chrome, Safari, Firefox, etc.).
- Enter the meeting link or use the meeting code to join.

### 4. Disable WebRTC in Firefox (Last Resort)
- Open Firefox.
- Type `about:config` in the Firefox address bar.
- Find the parameter `media.peerconnection.enabled` (you can search for it directly).
- Set it to **false**.
- Access the meeting via the link `kmeet.infomaniak.com`.

For more details, refer to the [Infomaniak support guide](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2441/fix-an-audio-issue-on-kmeet).

question: How do I create side rooms (breakout rooms) in kMeet?
ground_truth: To create side rooms in kMeet: 1) You must be a moderator. 2) Start kMeet via kmeet.infomaniak.com or app. 3) Once participants are in the meeting, click on the multi-user icon in the toolbar. 4) Click the button to add a side room. 5) Participants can then join or leave the room. 6) The moderator can force participants to join a specific side room via the action menu. Side rooms allow dividing a main meeting into several simultaneous discussions in distinct virtual spaces.
key_points: moderator can force participants to join
actual_response:
To create side rooms (breakout rooms) in kMeet, follow these steps:

### Prerequisites:
- You must be a moderator of the meeting to create and manage side rooms.

### Steps to Create a Side Room:
1. Start kMeet as a moderator via [kmeet.infomaniak.com](https://kmeet.infomaniak.com) or from one of the applications for computer or mobile devices.
2. Once the participants are in the meeting, click on the multi-user icon in the kMeet toolbar.
3. Click the button to add a side room.
4. Participants can then join the created room or leave it by displaying the menu with the same button as in step 2 above.
5. The moderator can also force one of the participants to join one of the side rooms by clicking on the action menu on the right in the list.

### Important Notes:
- Side rooms allow you to divide a main meeting into several simultaneous discussions in distinct virtual spaces.
- Only a moderator can create these rooms and manage participants between the main room and the subgroups.

For more details, refer to the [official guide](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2397/create-a-kmeet-meeting-side-room).

question: How can I record a kMeet meeting?
ground_truth: To record a kMeet meeting: Prerequisites: Have a kDrive, be the moderator, and don't use encrypted meeting with custom key. Steps: 1) Start kMeet. 2) Once in the meeting, click on the action menu (three dots). 3) Click 'Start recording'. 4) Log in to Infomaniak if needed and select a kDrive for storage. 5) To stop, click the toolbar again and choose 'Stop recording'. 6) The recording is saved to the kDrive root in .mp4 format when all participants leave. Maximum duration is 3 hours.
actual_response:
To record a kMeet meeting, follow these steps:

### Prerequisites:
- You must have a **kDrive** (standalone or as part of a kSuite).
- You must be the **moderator** of the video conference.
- The meeting must not be an **encrypted video conference with a custom key**.

### Steps to Record:
1. Start **kMeet** via [kmeet.infomaniak.com](https://kmeet.infomaniak.com) or from one of the apps for computers and mobile devices.
2. Once in the meeting, click on the action menu **○○○** in the kMeet toolbar.
3. Click on the icon ◉ **Start recording**.
4. Confirm the operation and, if necessary, log in to your Infomaniak account.
5. Select a kDrive to record the video conference on, then click the button to start.
6. To stop recording, click on the toolbar again and choose **Stop recording**.
7. Confirm, then choose whether you want to go to the recording location on kDrive.
8. The recording will be available at the root of the chosen kDrive as soon as the virtual room in which the meeting was held is closed (i.e., as soon as all participants have left the video conference).

### Technical Specifications:
- The recording is done on the server side and does not generate any load for the participant's computer.
- The recording is in **.mp4 video format**.
- The maximum duration of the recording is **3 hours**.

### Important Notes:
- The recording will only be available once the meeting is fully ended (all participants have left).
- Encrypted meetings with a custom key cannot be recorded.

For more details, refer to the [official documentation](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2472/save-a-kmeet-meeting-on-kdrive).

question: How do I set a password for my kMeet meeting?
ground_truth: To protect a kMeet meeting with a password: 1) Start kMeet via kmeet.infomaniak.com or app. 2) Start a new meeting. 3) Enter the meeting room name. 4) Click on 'security options'. 5) Enable the toggle switch to 'Protect access'. 6) Create the password. 7) Click Continue to start. 8) Share both the meeting link/code AND the password with participants. You can also enable end-to-end encryption from security options (works only with Chromium-based browsers).
actual_response:
To set a password for your kMeet meeting, follow these steps:

### Prerequisites:
- You must have access to kMeet via [kmeet.infomaniak.com](https://kmeet.infomaniak.com) or the kMeet application.

### Steps to Set a Password:
1. Start kMeet via [kmeet.infomaniak.com](https://kmeet.infomaniak.com) or from the kMeet application.
2. Start a new meeting.
3. Enter a name for your meeting room.
4. Click on the security options.
5. Enable the toggle switch to **Protect access**.
6. Create the password.
7. Continue to start the meeting.
8. Specify the name you want to use as a participant in the meeting.
9. Share the meeting link or code and the password with your participants.

### Additional Notes:
- You can review or re-display the password if necessary by inviting participants via the dedicated button.
- Ensure you share both the meeting link/code and the password with participants for them to join.

For more details, refer to the [official documentation](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2464/secure-a-kmeet-meeting-with-a-password-and-encryption-key).

question: How can I livestream a kMeet meeting?
ground_truth: To livestream a kMeet meeting: Prerequisites: Must be a moderator (no Video Streaming offer required). Steps: 1) Start kMeet via ksuite.infomaniak.com/kmeet or app. 2) Once in the meeting, click the action menu (three dots). 3) Choose 'Start live broadcast'. 4) Click 'Start' button. 5) Wait for Video Streaming to be created. 6) Copy the stream URL and share it with viewers. 7) A symbol and audio alert indicate the broadcast start. The stream is continuous for max 24 hours and stops when the kMeet meeting ends.
actual_response:
To livestream a kMeet meeting, follow these steps:

### Prerequisites:
- You must be a **moderator** of the kMeet meeting to create a live broadcast link.
- It is **not necessary** to own an Infomaniak Video Streaming offer to use this feature.

### Steps to Livestream:
1. Start the kMeet meeting via [ksuite.infomaniak.com/kmeet](https://ksuite.infomaniak.com/kmeet) or from the kMeet application on your computer or mobile device.
2. Once in the meeting, click on the action menu (**○○○**) in the kMeet toolbar.
3. Choose **Start live broadcast**.
4. Click the **Start** button to initiate the live stream.
5. Wait for the Video Streaming stream to be created.
6. Once the stream link is displayed, click the icon on the right to copy the URL.
7. Share the URL with participants or anyone who needs to attend the live broadcast.

### Important Notes:
- A symbol and an audible alert will indicate the start of the broadcast.
- The stream is broadcast continuously for a **maximum of 24 hours**.
- The stream **will no longer be accessible** once the kMeet meeting is stopped.

### Advantages of Live Streaming:
- Large-scale public broadcasting without restricting access to invited participants.
- Suitable for conferences, webinars, or live events with hundreds or thousands of viewers.
- No need to manage access for each participant; the stream is viewable via a simple link.
- Passive access for viewers without requiring registration or interaction.
- Higher broadcast resolution compared to kMeet, which may be limited by bandwidth constraints.

For more details, refer to the [official guide](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1355/broadcast-a-kmeet-meeting-via-live-streaming-mode).

question: How do I install kDrive on Linux?
ground_truth: To install kDrive on Linux: Prerequisites: Download the kDrive .AppImage file, install libfuse2 (required for Ubuntu 23.04+: sudo apt install libfuse2), D-Bus, and gnome-keyring or kwallet. Steps: 1) Place the .AppImage file in an 'Applications' folder. 2) Right-click the file and select 'Permissions'. 3) Check 'Allow executing file as a program'. Note: Officially supported on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS+ with GNOME or KDE. Lite Sync and right-click context menu not available on Linux. For Ubuntu startup, add to 'Startup Application Preferences'. For GNOME icon, install AppIndicator extension.
key_points: Lite Sync not available on Linux
actual_response:
To install kDrive on Linux, follow these steps:

### Prerequisites:
- Ensure you have a Linux system that meets the requirements:
  - Officially supported systems: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (or later) with GNOME or KDE desktop environments.
  - Infomaniak does not provide support for other Linux distributions or desktop environments.
- Download the kDrive desktop app for Linux (file type: .AppImage).
- Ensure you have the following dependencies installed:
  - Fuse2 (required to run AppImage):
    - For Ubuntu 23.04 and later, install Fuse2 using the command:
      ```bash
      sudo apt install libfuse2
      ```
  - D-Bus
  - Gnome-keyring or kwallet (usually pre-installed except on some lightweight distributions).

### Steps to Install:
1. **Prepare the AppImage File:**
   - Place the downloaded `.AppImage` file in a folder, for example, "Applications."
   - Right-click on the file and select **Permissions**.
   - Check the box **"Allow executing file as a program."**

2. **Run the AppImage:**
   - Double-click the `.AppImage` file to launch the kDrive installer.
   - Follow the on-screen instructions to complete the installation.

3. **Additional Configuration (Optional):**
   - **Ubuntu:** To run kDrive at startup, add the file to "Startup Application Preferences."
   - **GNOME:** If the icon is missing, install the [AppIndicator extension](https://extensions.gnome.org/extension/615/appindicator-support/).

### Platform Limitations:
- Some kDrive features are not available on Linux, such as:
  - **Lite Sync** option.
  - **Right-click context menu**.

### Technical Specifications:
- The kDrive app is designed to work on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS or later with GNOME or KDE desktop environments.

### Important Notes:
- Ensure all permissions and dependencies are correctly configured for the app to function properly.
- If you encounter issues, verify that Fuse2 and other dependencies are installed.

For more details, refer to the [official guide](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/617/install-kdrive-on-linux).

question: How can I share a file from kDrive?
ground_truth: To share a file/folder in kDrive: 1) Access kDrive web app at ksuite.infomaniak.com/kdrive. 2) Right-click on the file/folder. 3) Click 'Share...' at the top of the menu. Options: a) Activate a public share link (with options for modification, expiration date, password, download authorization). b) Or enter a kDrive user, contact email, or work team. For each person, define rights: 'viewing', 'modification', or 'management'. Recipients without Infomaniak account can create one free. Warning: deactivating/reactivating public link changes the URL.
key_points: recipients can create free Infomaniak account
actual_response:
To share a file from kDrive, follow these steps:

### Prerequisites:
- You must have access to kDrive.

### Steps to Share a File or Folder:
1. Access the [kDrive Web app](https://ksuite.infomaniak.com/kdrive).
2. Right-click on the file or folder you want to share.
3. Click on **Share** at the top of the dropdown menu.

From there, you have two options:

#### Option 1: Create a Public Share Link
- Activate the **public share link**.
- Customize the sharing options:
  - Allow modifications (if the file is in a collaborative format).
  - Set an expiration date.
  - Add a password.
  - Allow or restrict downloads.
  - Enable users to request full access.
- Copy the link to share it or send it directly from the sharing window.

#### Option 2: Share with Specific Users
- Enter the email address of a kDrive user, a contact from your address book, or a [Work Team](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2585) if sharing within "Organization Folders."
- Choose the level of access (view, modify, etc.).

### Important Notes:
- Deactivating and reactivating the public share link changes the URL and invalidates the previous one.
- For files like Word, Excel, or PowerPoint, you can allow online editing without requiring an Infomaniak account.
- You can request access from the shared file page by enabling the **"Add files"** button in the advanced sharing settings.

### Related Actions:
- You can modify or disable the share link at any time.
- For folders in "Organization Folders," you can share with external users who will need to sign up or log in to access the content.

For more details, refer to the [kDrive sharing guide](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2382/share-data-from-the-kdrive-web-app).

question: What is a Drop Box in kDrive and how do I create one?
ground_truth: A Drop Box in kDrive lets you invite contacts to deposit files/folders directly into your kDrive. To create: 1) Access kDrive at ksuite.infomaniak.com/kdrive. 2) Navigate to the folder that will host the data (personal or shared). 3) Click the blue 'New' button. 4) Click 'Drop Box'. 5) Enter a name. 6) Choose access settings. 7) Click 'Create'. 8) Share the link with contacts. Advanced options: email notification on deposit, password protection, expiration date, storage limit. To disable: go to Shares > Drop boxes, right-click and select 'Disable' (converts to regular folder).
key_points: can set password, expiration, storage limit
actual_response:
A **Drop Box** in kDrive is a feature that allows you to create a designated folder where external contacts can upload files or folders directly into your kDrive. This is useful for collecting content from others without granting them full access to your kDrive. The files uploaded by your contacts are automatically organized in the specified location within your kDrive.

### How to Create a Drop Box in kDrive

To create a Drop Box in kDrive, follow these steps:

1. **Access kDrive**:
   - [Click here](https://ksuite.infomaniak.com/kdrive) to access the Infomaniak kDrive Web app.

2. **Navigate to the Desired Folder**:
   - Browse through the kDrive directory in the left sidebar.
   - Choose the folder where you want the Drop Box to be created:
     - **My Folder**: If the data is private and specific to your user.
     - **Organization Folders**: If you want other users in your kDrive to view the data from the Drop Box.

3. **Create the Drop Box**:
   - Click the blue **New** button in the directory where you want the Drop Box.
   - Select **Drop Box** from the menu.

4. **Configure the Drop Box**:
   - Enter a **name** for the Drop Box.
   - The full path to the Drop Box location within your kDrive will be displayed for your reference.
   - Depending on your kDrive plan and the folder location, you can choose to restrict access to only your user or allow other users in the Organization Folder to access it.

5. **Finalize the Creation**:
   - Click the blue **Create** button to create the Drop Box.

### Additional Options for Drop Boxes

- **Share the Drop Box**:
  - You can share the link to the Drop Box or send it via email to your contacts.
  - Advanced options allow you to:
    - Receive email notifications when files are uploaded.
    - Protect the folder with a password.
    - Set an expiration date for the Drop Box.
    - Limit the storage space of the Drop Box.
    - Customize the appearance of the Drop Box.

### Managing Drop Boxes

- **Disable or Modify a Drop Box**:
  - To disable or modify a Drop Box, go to the **Shares** section in the left sidebar.
  - Click on **Drop boxes**.
  - Right-click or use the action menu **⋮** next to the Drop Box you want to manage.
  - Choose **Disable** to deactivate the share link without deleting the existing data (the box will become a simple folder).
  - Select **Settings** to modify advanced options like notifications, password protection, or storage limits.

### Prerequisites and Limitations

- **Prerequisites**:
  - You must have access to kDrive and the necessary permissions to create and manage Drop Boxes.
- **Platform Limitations**:
  - Drop Boxes are managed via the kDrive Web app and are not specific to any platform (Windows, macOS, Linux, etc.).
- **User Role Requirements**:
  - You must have the appropriate rights to create and manage Drop Boxes in the selected folder (e.g., administrator or owner rights for Organization Folders).
- **Important Notes**:
  - Files uploaded to a Drop Box are directly stored in the specified location within your kDrive.
  - Disabling a Drop Box will not delete the files already uploaded; it will only deactivate the share link.

For more details, refer to the [official documentation](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2386/manage-kdrive-drop-boxes).

question: How do I resolve sync conflicts in kDrive?
ground_truth: Sync conflicts occur when: a file is modified locally AND on kDrive Web simultaneously, or during conflicting create/move operations. Resolution: kDrive Web version is kept, local version is saved as '[filename]_conflict'. Options: 1) Keep both (only original syncs). 2) Delete _conflict if it's older. 3) Delete original and rename _conflict to sync it. 4) Manually merge then delete _conflict. To view conflicts: click kDrive icon > info button > view events. From version 3.6.11, locally modified files are moved to 'kDrive Rescue Folder' instead of deleted. Avoid conflicts by not working on the same file with multiple people.
key_points: conflicts when same file modified locally and online
can keep both, delete, or merge
actual_response:
To resolve sync conflicts in kDrive, follow these steps:

### How to Display Conflicts
1. **Left-click** on the kDrive desktop app icon in your computer's notification area:
   - Top right on macOS
   - Bottom right on Windows
   - Double left-click in the taskbar on Linux
2. Click on the information button at the top.
3. Click on the listed event to view its details.
4. Conflicts and errors are displayed in two distinct tabs, allowing you to identify unsynchronized data.

### Resolving Conflicts
1. Choose how to resolve the conflict:
   - **Send the local version to the server**: This will synchronize the local version.
   - **Send the local version to the computer's recycle bin**: This will discard the local version.

### Handling Conflict Files
- The kDrive Web version is kept as is.
- Your local version is saved as "[file name]_conflict".
- The conflicting file is not synchronized with kDrive Web.

### What to Do with Conflict Files
- **Keep both versions**: Only the original file will synchronize.
- **Delete the `_conflict` file**: If it is the least recent version.
- **Delete the original version**: If it is obsolete, then rename the `_conflict` file to synchronize it.
- **Manually merge the two versions**: Before deleting the `_conflict` file.

### Avoiding Synchronization Conflicts
- Do not work on the same file with multiple people (unless working online on a Word, Excel, or PowerPoint document).
- Synchronize your offline modifications before modifying the same files online.
- Avoid creating folders with the same name as folders you do not synchronize on a device.

### Manual Resolution of Conflicts
1. **Open** both files.
2. **Compare** the differences.
3. **Retrieve** the information from the conflict file (the one with the exclamation mark) into the base file.
4. **Delete** the conflict file that is not synchronized (the one with the exclamation mark and the note `conflicted copy`).

### Important Notes
- Conflict files (with the exclamation mark and the note `conflicted copy` in their name) are not synchronized.
- Refer to [this guide](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2153) if you encounter a problem even though the kDrive desktop app icon is green.

For more details, refer to the [official documentation](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2403/resolve-a-kdrive-synchronization-conflict).

question: How do I manage user rights in kDrive?
ground_truth: kDrive has 2 permission levels: 1) Administrator - same rights as owner (sharing, statistics, restore/delete folders, import data, access all files). 2) User - access folders at root, create/share content, but cannot manage product, view statistics, or create root folders. To modify: 1) Go to ksuite.infomaniak.com/kdrive. 2) Click action menu next to the kDrive. 3) Click 'Manage users'. 4) Select user and choose access level. Note: Don't confuse Manager rights (product management) with kDrive rights (data access). A user can have restricted Manager rights but be Administrator in kDrive.
key_points: don't confuse Manager rights with kDrive rights
actual_response:
To manage user rights in kDrive, follow these steps:

### Prerequisites:
- You must be an **Administrator** or **Legal Representative** within the Organization to manage user rights.
- The user must be added as a **collaborator** in the Organization.

### Steps to Manage User Rights:

1. **Access User Management:**
   - Go to the [Infomaniak Manager](https://manager.infomaniak.com/v3/ng/accounts/rights/users/list).
   - Click on the action menu **⋮** next to the user you want to manage.
   - Select **Edit product access**.

2. **Grant Access to kDrive:**
   - Expand the tabs/accordions by product if necessary.
   - Click on the **kDrive** product category.
   - Select the relevant kDrive product(s).
   - Decide whether future additional products should automatically be visible to the user and with what type of permissions (Technical/Statistical).
   - Click **Save**.

3. **Modify Permissions in kDrive:**
   - Access the [kDrive Web app](https://ksuite.infomaniak.com/kdrive).
   - Select the relevant kDrive from the dropdown menu in the left sidebar.
   - Click on the action menu **⋮** next to the user in question.
   - Select **Manage users**.
   - Adjust the user's permissions as needed (e.g., Administrator, Editor, Viewer).

4. **Advanced Actions:**
   - If necessary, use the action menu **⋮** for advanced actions such as blocking access, removing the user, or viewing their activity.

### Important Notes:
- **Technical Rights:** Allow the user to access the dashboard and manage technical details.
- **Statistical Rights:** Grant access to storage statistics, active users, and activity logs.
- **External Users:** External users do not have access to shared calendars and address books within the Organization.

### Related Actions:
- You can also manage permissions related to actions on [categories](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2628).
- If a modification is not possible, ensure the user's role is not set to **Administrator** at the Organization level.

For more details, refer to the [Infomaniak documentation](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2365/manage-a-kdrive-users-rights).

question: How can I access kDrive files locally without downloading them?
ground_truth: To access kDrive files locally: 1) Install the kDrive desktop app. 2) Click on the kDrive icon in notification area (top right macOS, bottom right Windows, double-click on Linux). 3) Click action menu at top right. 4) Choose 'Open kDrive Web' to access server files. 5) Or click the item above to open the local folder. Files can be physically present or virtually present (if Lite Sync is enabled). Lite Sync allows files to appear locally without taking up disk space - they download on demand when opened.
key_points: Open kDrive Web for server files
actual_response:
To access kDrive files locally without downloading them, you can use the **Lite Sync** feature on the kDrive desktop app for Windows or macOS. This feature allows you to virtually store your kDrive files on your computer, making them accessible without taking up local storage space. Here’s how it works:

### **Lite Sync Feature**
- **Purpose**: Saves space by storing files virtually on your computer. Files are only downloaded when you need to access them.
- **Accessibility**: Files are always accessible via the kDrive web app, but locally, they are "dehydrated" and require an internet connection to fully access.
- **Compatibility**: Works on Windows and macOS (not available on Linux).
- **Scope**: Applies to an entire kDrive or advanced synchronization, and is specific to your kDrive app (other users can make different choices).

### **How to Enable Lite Sync**
1. Install the kDrive desktop app on your Windows or macOS device.
2. Log in to your Infomaniak account and select the kDrive you want to synchronize.
3. During setup, you will be prompted to enable or disable the **Lite Sync** option.
4. Enable **Lite Sync** to virtually store files on your computer.

### **Free Up Space**
- Once Lite Sync is enabled, you can manually free up space for specific folders or subfolders:
  1. Navigate to the folder in Windows Explorer or macOS Finder.
  2. Right-click the folder and select **Free up space** under the kDrive options.
- **Note**: This action does not apply by default to new files or folders added locally.

### **Important Considerations**
- **Storage Space**: If you enable Lite Sync for a large kDrive, ensure you have enough free space on your hard drive, as the feature may require significant space initially.
- **Internet Connection**: Files are only fully accessible with an internet connection.
- **Platform Limitations**: Lite Sync is not available on Linux.

### **Source**
For more details, refer to the [official documentation](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2562/manage-the-lite-sync-kdrive-option-windows).

question: How do I sync kDrive with my Synology NAS?

To sync kDrive with your Synology NAS, follow these steps:

### Prerequisites:
- Have a Synology NAS accessible from the Internet.

### Steps to Sync kDrive and Synology via Cloud Sync:

2. If necessary, download and install the **Cloud Sync** app from the **Package Center**.
3. Open **Cloud Sync**.

   - Password: Create an application password for this specific use.

   - **Download only remote changes**: Ideal for saving a kDrive to your NAS.

question: How do I create a channel in kChat?
ground_truth: To create a channel in kChat: 1) Click the button in the left sidebar of kChat web app (ksuite.infomaniak.com/kchat). 2) Click 'Create a new channel'. 3) Set: A) Name (modifiable later), B) URL (lowercase, numbers, dots, dashes, underscores), C) Private or Public status, D) Description. Every Organization has a default 'General' channel for all users. Public channels are visible to all; Private channels require invitation. To convert public to private: click channel > chevron > Convert (permanent). To leave: chevron > Leave. To archive: chevron > Archive. Can also add to favorites, mute, or organize by categories.
actual_response:
To create a channel in kChat, follow these steps:

### How to Create a Channel in kChat

1. Open the **kChat** web app (online service [ksuite.infomaniak.com/kchat](https://ksuite.infomaniak.com/kchat)).
2. Click on the **+** button located in the left sidebar.
3. Select **Create a new channel**.

### Information Related to a Channel

When creating a new channel, you can customize the following:

- **Name**: The name of the channel, which can be modified later.
- **URL**: By default, it uses the channel name, but you can modify it using lowercase letters, numbers, dots, dashes, and underscores. This can also be changed later.
- **Status**: Choose whether the channel is **PRIVATE** or **PUBLIC**. This setting can also be modified later.

### Additional Notes

- A **General Channel** exists by default in every Organization on kChat, and all users are automatically invited to it.
- Private channels, as well as public and guest channels, are limited in number based on your kSuite offer. Refer to the comparison table on the sales page for more information.

For more details, you can refer to the [official documentation](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2732/manage-a-kchat-channel).

question: What slash commands are available in kChat?
ground_truth: To use slash commands in kChat: 1) Click in the composition field. 2) Type / followed by the command. 3) Send. Typing just / shows available commands in a modal (like going offline). You can create custom slash commands: 1) Open kChat web or desktop app. 2) Click 'New' icon next to organization name. 3) Click 'Integrations'. 4) Click 'Slash command'. 5) Add a command with name, trigger, content type, and action. Custom commands can call external APIs or run scripts. Note: External users cannot see the Integrations menu.
actual_response:
Here are the details about slash commands in kChat:

### How to Use Slash Commands
To execute a slash command on kChat:
1. Click in the composition field within a channel.
2. Enter a `/` (slash or forward slash) followed by the command.
3. Confirm to send the command.

If you type only the `/` sign, a modal will appear displaying the available commands, such as going offline.

### Creating Custom Slash Commands
**Prerequisites:**
- You must not be an external user (external users will not see the *Integrations* menu).

**Steps to Create a Custom Slash Command:**
1. Access the **Web kChat** app or open the **desktop kChat** app.
2. Click on the **New** icon next to your kChat organization name.
3. Click on **Integrations**.
4. Click on **Slash command**.
5. Click the blue button to **Add a command**.
6. Configure the slash command (name, trigger, expected content type, action to execute, etc.).
7. Save the command.
8. Test the command to ensure it works as expected.

**Important Notes:**
- Creating custom slash commands may require additional programming skills, especially for integrating custom features or interactions with external systems.
- Follow security best practices when creating these commands to avoid potential security vulnerabilities.

### Permissions for External Users
- External users (guests) can use slash commands, except for restricted commands such as inviting members, renaming channels, or modifying headers.

For more details, refer to the [kChat slash commands guide](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2134).

question: How can I connect external applications to kChat?
ground_truth: To connect external apps to kChat using webhooks: 1) Open kChat web or desktop app. 2) Click 'New' icon next to organization name. 3) Click 'Integrations'. 4) Access webhook categories. For incoming webhooks (receive messages from external apps): 1) Click 'Incoming Webhooks'. 2) Add name and description. 3) Select destination channel. 4) Save to get URL. 5) External app sends POST request with JSON: {"text": "message"}. For outgoing webhooks: kChat sends info when events occur. Parameters include channel override, username, icon_url. Response includes message details. Add ?slack_return_format=true for Slack-style response.

### What is Euria and how do I use it in kChat?

**Euria** is an artificial intelligence integrated into **kSuite**, specifically designed to assist users within **kChat**. It can perform tasks such as calculations, translations, providing information, and answering questions. Euria is also capable of summarizing discussions in kChat, making it a powerful tool for productivity and collaboration.

---

### How to Use Euria in kChat

#### Add Euria to Your kChat Contacts
Euria is already available as a bot in your kChat contacts. If you don't see it yet, follow these steps:

1. Click on the channel search in the left sidebar of kChat (bots appear as channels).
2. Alternatively, click the **+** icon next to **Direct Messages** to search for the bot.
3. Look for bots labeled with the tag **[bot]** or search for terms like *bot* or *chat*.
4. Add the bot to your contacts.

> **Note:** Do not create a group conversation with the bot. Instead, create a private discussion channel between yourself and the bot.

Once added, you can interact with Euria by sending messages as if you were chatting with a colleague.

---

#### Summarize a Discussion Using Euria
Euria can automatically summarize discussions in kChat. Here’s how to use this feature:

1. Hover over the message you want to summarize.
2. Select the Euria actions icon in the top right of the message.
3. Click on **Summarize the discussion thread**.
4. The summary, generated by AI, will be sent by the kChat Bot in the right sidebar.

---

### Important Notes
- Euria sends a welcome message to new users in kChat.
- You can disable daily reminders sent by Euria by following the steps in [this guide](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1622).
- For more details on the AI model used and the responsibilities of each party, refer to [this guide](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1369).

---

### Prerequisites
- You must have access to **kChat** within **kSuite**.
- Euria is available by default in kChat, but you may need to add it to your contacts if it’s not visible.

---

### Platform Limitations
- No specific platform limitations are mentioned for Euria in kChat. It should work across all platforms where kChat is available.

---

### Technical Specifications
- Euria can summarize discussions and provide AI-generated responses.
- It integrates seamlessly with kChat for real-time interactions.

---

### User Role Requirements
- No specific role requirements are mentioned. Any user with access to kChat can interact with Euria.

---

### Related Actions
- You can disable daily reminders sent by Euria if you no longer wish to receive them.
- Euria can also be used to perform calculations, translations, and provide information on various topics.

---

For further assistance or details, refer to the official documentation:
- [Use Euria on kChat (Conversational Agent)](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2840)
- [Use Euria on kChat (Summarize a Discussion)](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2480)
